measures.what: Please report the tripod brand/model and camera model, and describe the empty mounting socket: does it have a sliding dovetail with a locking knob, a shaped pocket with a latch, or just a threaded stud? If possible, include the socket's approximate length and width in mm. Don't force anything into it.
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes); camera socket thread: 1/4-20 (the usual camera thread)

measures.item: tripod clamp and salvaged webcam-mount bolt
measures.what: Can you confirm whether the clamp has two opposing sloped jaws, one tightened by a knob (Arca-style)? Measure the jaw's sloped gripping height and the narrower opening between the upper lips when set for a 38 mm plate, plus usable jaw length. For the salvaged 1/4-20 webcam bolt, measure head diameter, head thickness, and length from under its head to its tip; say whether the underside of its head is flat. Also gently measure the usable camera socket depth with a nonmetallic probe, without tightening a screw into it. If any measurement isn't possible, say so.
measures.reply: webcam bolt head across: about 15 mm (its head); webcam bolt head height: about 5 mm (its head); webcam bolt length: about 10 mm (under the head); tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above; tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.item: tripod clamp, webcam bolt, and camera
measures.what: A few fit-critical details are still missing: (1) vertical height of the angled jaw gripping face, (2) gap between the TOP inner edges of the lips when the bottom fits a 38 mm plate, and (3) length along those jaws. If you cannot measure these, explicitly say which ones—you can still print a small unladen fit test, but I won't treat it as camera-safe.
